Frequently Asked Questions

Information on frequently asked questions.

Where can I see my tax bill?

View my tax bill

Where can I see what I paid?

Please contact our office via phone at: (208) 287-6800 or email us: [email protected]

Do I have the homestead exemption?

Your consolidated property tax bill will reflect your homestead exemption, or your can view that information on the Assessor’s website.

What time period did my June payment cover?

Property values in Idaho are assessed as of January 1 and billed and due later that same year. For example, values assessed on January 1, are used to determine your taxes that will be billed in November and due in December.

The full year’s taxes are due in December. However, state law allows taxpayers to pay in full or in two installments, provided the first installment is paid on time.*

First installment: Due in December of the same year the taxes are billed.

If the December installment is not paid by the deadline, a 2% late charge is added, along with interest at 1% per month beginning January 1 following the due date.

Second installment: Due the following June (this payment is the remaining balance of that same tax year’s bill).

If the June installment is not paid by the deadline, a 2% late charge is added, along with interest at 1% per month beginning January 1 of the current year.

While these are often referred to as “half” payments, both installments apply to the same tax year’s assessment.

For the 2025 tax year, bills are issued by the fourth Monday in November 2025, with the following due dates:

Important: This schedule applies only to the Primary Tax Bill.

Payment Due Date Applies to:
Full Payment December 20, 2025 Total amount of the 2025 property tax bill
1st installment December 20, 2025 1st half of 2025 taxes (January – June 2025)
2nd installment June 20, 2026 2nd half of 2025 taxes (July – December 2025)

*Note: Payments are applied to the oldest tax balance first. If your property taxes are delinquent, the payments shown in this table may not reflect how your payment will be applied.

If you have questions about how a payment will be applied to your parcel, please contact our office at 208-287-6800.

How can I change my mailing address?

Please visit the Assessor’s page: Assessor’s Change of Mailing Address Request Form.

How can I apply for Property Tax Assistance?

Property Tax Reduction (Circuit Breaker)

To apply for Property Tax Reduction or Circuit Breaker, please apply through the Assessor’s Office between January 1 and April 15 of the tax year. For more information, please call the Ada County Assessor’s Office at (208) 287-7200 or view the Property Tax Reduction Brochure.

100% Disable Veteran's Assistance

To apply for 100% Service-Connected Disabled Veteran’s Assistance, please apply through the Assessor’s Office between January 1 and April 15 of the tax year. For more information, please call the Ada County Assessor’s Office at (208) 287-7200.

Hardship Application

If you have experienced difficulty paying your property taxes, you may qualify for a reduction or cancellation of your property taxes. For more information, please call the Ada County Indigent Services at (208) 287-7960.

Property Tax Deferral

To apply for Property Tax Deferral, please apply through the Assessor’s Office by September 3, 2024. For more information, please call the Ada County Assessor’s Office at (208) 287-7200 or call the Idaho State Tax Commission at (208) 334-7660.
